contracts.text: Bind only to 127.0.0.1; GET / serves web/index.html. Files referenced by that page are served from web/ at their corresponding root-relative paths with appropriate content types. The page and assets require no external network access or build step.

GET /api/items returns 200 JSON as an array of objects with id, name, quantity, unit, expires and created_at. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD; absent expiry is null. Sort by expiry ascending, nulls last, with id ascending as the tie-breaker. Optional q is a case-insensitive literal substring of name; optional expiring_within is a nonnegative integer number of days and includes expired items and items expiring through that many calendar days from local today, excluding null expiry. Filters combine. Invalid query input returns 400 JSON {"error":"..."}. UI uses same-origin requests and handles a non-success response or network failure visibly.
Later wave: agree on item creation, updates, consumption, deletion, validation errors and atomic concurrency.

pantry_db.py exposes init_db(db_path) and create_item(db_path, fields). init_db creates the schema if absent and preserves existing data. create_item validates and atomically inserts one item into that same schema and returns its item dictionary, including id and created_at. fields is a dict with required name and quantity and optional unit and expires; omitted unit defaults to "" and omitted expires to None. Name is a nonblank string of 1–80 characters, quantity is an integer >= 0 excluding booleans, unit is a string, and expires is None or a real YYYY-MM-DD calendar date. Unknown fields or invalid values raise ValueError with a human-readable message and insert nothing; storage failures propagate. The importer converts CSV quantity text to an integer and an empty expiry to None before calling create_item, counts conversion or ValueError failures as skipped rows, and does not treat storage failures as invalid rows. The server uses this same initialization, validation and insertion boundary.

In a fresh project folder, place server.py and pantry_db.py at the root and the page at web/index.html with its local assets under web/. From that root run python server.py --port PORT --db PATH; the server creates or opens the SQLite file at PATH and serves http://127.0.0.1:PORT/. GET /api/items returns the JSON array defined by item-list. The page behavior for populated and empty arrays is defined by list-presentation. Use only supplied local files and Python 3.12 standard library at runtime.

On loading /, request GET /api/items from the same origin. For a populated array, visibly render each item's name and quantity; for an empty array, visibly show an empty-pantry message. Keep the page usable and show a visible error if the request fails.

decisions.choice: Use a same-origin JSON API and serve local page assets directly from web/.
decisions.reason: This enables an offline vertical slice without a build step or cross-origin setup.

decisions.choice: Treat the seven-day window as inclusive of expired items through local today plus seven calendar days.

scopeIn: Build ShelfLife, a small local pantry tracker for one household. Python 3.12 standard library only (sqlite3, http.server, csv, json); no third-party packages, no network access at runtime, no build step.
Backend: `python server.py --port PORT --db PATH` serves a JSON API and the web UI on 127.0.0.1.
Items have: id, name (1-80 chars), quantity (integer >= 0), unit (text, optional), expires (YYYY-MM-DD or null), created_at.
GET /api/items (optional ?expiring_within=DAYS, ?q=TEXT name search) returns items sorted by expiry (nulls last).

POST /api/items creates; PATCH /api/items/{id} updates quantity/name/unit/expires; POST /api/items/{id}/consume {"amount": n} reduces quantity (never below 0; 409 if amount exceeds quantity); DELETE /api/items/{id}.

Invalid input returns 400 with {"error": "..."}; unknown id 404. Data persists in the SQLite file across restarts. Concurrent requests must not corrupt data or lose updates (two simultaneous consumes of the last unit: exactly one succeeds).
UI (served at /): one responsive page that works at phone and desktop sizes.

"Expiring soon" section (next 7 days, expired items clearly marked), full list with search and an expiry filter, add-item form with inline validation messages, consume and delete actions, empty state and a visible error state when the API fails.
Keyboard accessible with visible focus; readable contrast; no horizontal scrolling at 375px. Clean, calm visual design.

Import: `python import_items.py FILE.csv --db PATH` loads rows (name,quantity,unit,expires) into the same database, skipping invalid rows and printing one summary line "imported N, skipped M" (exit 0), or exit 2 with an error on an unreadable file.
Done means: the server, UI and importer work together from a fresh folder; a short README explains how to run them.
scopeOut: Multiple households, accounts, synchronization, and hosted deployment.
Third-party packages, runtime network dependencies, and a build pipeline.
Additional pantry features beyond the specified API, UI, and CSV import.

facts.Design guidance used by UI workers: For a UI, follow the accepted visual direction with deliberate typography, spacing, contrast, clear language and purposeful accessible interaction. Inspect the real result. A UI must look designed by someone with a point of view, following the accepted visual direction. Avoid the default AI look: a system-font stack as the whole typography, a centered column on off-white, a generic pill button, purple gradients, cards in cards, gray text on color, bounce easing. Instead: deliberate type with real hierarchy from fonts available offline; a confident palette with strong contrast; generous rhythm in spacing; motion that is brief, purposeful and honors reduced-motion; words a person would actually say. No TODOs, no partial implementations. A finished page opens with a clean browser console: give it an icon (for example <link rel="icon" href="data:,">) and serve every file it requests.

body.instructions: Implement the thin read-only vertical slice using local assets without a build step or external network access. Follow the page-serving, item-list, list-presentation, and fresh-folder-integration contracts; use forest green, warm cream, restrained harvest orange, offline-available typography, and generous spacing. Check populated, empty, and failed requests and responsive keyboard usability, including the real server-to-page integration when the contracted server files are available. Leave mutations, search, expiry filtering, and their controls for a later wave.

body.acceptance: The local pantry page displays the current item list or an understandable empty or error state on phone and desktop screens.
body.story: As a household member, I want to see the contents of my pantry when I open ShelfLife.

body.acceptance: Opening the page requests the same-origin item list and visibly shows every returned item's name and quantity, or an empty-pantry message when there are no items.
If the item-list request fails or returns a non-success response, the page remains usable and visibly explains that the pantry could not be loaded.
The page is readable and keyboard usable at phone and desktop widths, has visible focus and no horizontal scrolling at 375 pixels, and uses the agreed offline pantry-led visual style.

body.choice: Use a same-origin JSON API and serve local page assets directly from web/.
body.reason: This enables an offline vertical slice without a build step or cross-origin setup.

body.choice: Treat the seven-day window as inclusive of expired items through local today plus seven calendar days.
body.reason: The page must show upcoming expiries and clearly mark expired items.

body.choice: Keep one backend-owned persistence and validation implementation for both server and importer.
body.reason: A canonical producer boundary prevents the importer and API from disagreeing about valid records or database layout.

body.responsibility: Own the local HTTP server, item persistence, validation, and API concurrency.

body.text: In a fresh project folder, place server.py and pantry_db.py at the root and the page at web/index.html with its local assets under web/. From that root run python server.py --port PORT --db PATH; the server creates or opens the SQLite file at PATH and serves http://127.0.0.1:PORT/. GET /api/items returns the JSON array defined by item-list. The page behavior for populated and empty arrays is defined by list-presentation. Use only supplied local files and Python 3.12 standard library at runtime.

body.instructions:
The page is absent from your worktree and no contract names its fields. Write docs/try-it.md and declare a docs/try-it/ WAVE-VERIFY check from contracts: start with temporary data, open the page, import/API, check the promised text, save a screenshot to SELDON_EVIDENCE_DIR, and stop what you started; leave unseen forms to the page owner's check.
This wave: Run the thinnest offline vertical slice: start the server against SQLite, load the responsive page, and display the real item-list response, including an empty pantry.

body.responsibility: Own CSV import, fresh-folder instructions, and end-to-end integration checks.

body.text: GET /api/items returns 200 JSON as an array of objects with id, name, quantity, unit, expires and created_at. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD; absent expiry is null. Sort by expiry ascending, nulls last, with id ascending as the tie-breaker. Optional q is a case-insensitive literal substring of name; optional expiring_within is a nonnegative integer number of days and includes expired items and items expiring through that many calendar days from local today, excluding null expiry. Filters combine. Invalid query input returns 400 JSON {"error":"..."}. UI uses same-origin requests and handles a non-success response or network failure visibly.
Later wave: agree on item creation, updates, consumption, deletion, validation errors and atomic concurrency.

On loading /, request GET /api/items from the same origin. For a populated array, visibly render each item's name and quantity; for an empty array, visibly show an empty-pantry message. Keep the page usable and show a visible error if the request fails.

Bind only to 127.0.0.1; GET / serves web/index.html. Files referenced by that page are served from web/ at their corresponding root-relative paths with appropriate content types. The page and assets require no external network access or build step.

body.text: pantry_db.py exposes init_db(db_path) and create_item(db_path, fields). init_db creates the schema if absent and preserves existing data. create_item validates and atomically inserts one item into that same schema and returns its item dictionary, including id and created_at. fields is a dict with required name and quantity and optional unit and expires; omitted unit defaults to "" and omitted expires to None. Name is a nonblank string of 1–80 characters, quantity is an integer >= 0 excluding booleans, unit is a string, and expires is None or a real YYYY-MM-DD calendar date. Unknown fields or invalid values raise ValueError with a human-readable message and insert nothing; storage failures propagate. The importer converts CSV quantity text to an integer and an empty expiry to None before calling create_item, counts conversion or ValueError failures as skipped rows, and does not treat storage failures as invalid rows. The server uses this same initialization, validation and insertion boundary.

scopeIn: Build ShelfLife, a small local pantry tracker for one household. Python 3.12 standard library only (sqlite3, http.server, csv, json); no third-party packages, no network access at runtime, no build step.
Backend: `python server.py --port PORT --db PATH` serves a JSON API and the web UI on 127.0.0.1.
Items have: id, name (1-80 chars), quantity (integer >= 0), unit (text, optional), expires (YYYY-MM-DD or null), created_at.
GET /api/items (optional ?expiring_within=DAYS, ?q=TEXT name search) returns items sorted by expiry (nulls last).

POST /api/items creates; PATCH /api/items/{id} updates quantity/name/unit/expires; POST /api/items/{id}/consume {"amount": n} reduces quantity (never below 0; 409 if amount exceeds quantity); DELETE /api/items/{id}.

Invalid input returns 400 with {"error": "..."}; unknown id 404. Data persists in the SQLite file across restarts. Concurrent requests must not corrupt data or lose updates (two simultaneous consumes of the last unit: exactly one succeeds).
UI (served at /): one responsive page that works at phone and desktop sizes.

"Expiring soon" section (next 7 days, expired items clearly marked), full list with search and an expiry filter, add-item form with inline validation messages, consume and delete actions, empty state and a visible error state when the API fails.
Keyboard accessible with visible focus; readable contrast; no horizontal scrolling at 375px. Clean, calm visual design.

Import: `python import_items.py FILE.csv --db PATH` loads rows (name,quantity,unit,expires) into the same database, skipping invalid rows and printing one summary line "imported N, skipped M" (exit 0), or exit 2 with an error on an unreadable file.
Done means: the server, UI and importer work together from a fresh folder; a short README explains how to run them.
scopeOut: Multiple households, accounts, synchronization, and hosted deployment.
Third-party packages, runtime network dependencies, and a build pipeline.
Additional pantry features beyond the specified API, UI, and CSV import.
body.understanding: A dependable, private local pantry tracker that makes it easy for one household to see what needs attention and keep quantities current.
users: Members of one household managing a shared local pantry.
